# Lunde et al.

Lunde et al. refers to the authors of a 2018 research publication cited in the AFDK (Atrieflimren i Danmark) quality program documentation. The work is referenced to support the claim that atrial fibrillation (AF) is a complex disease that affects patients differently, and that healthcare professionals must therefore recognize each patient's individual starting point for acquiring learning and skills [^src1].

The citation appears in a chapter of the AFDK 2024 report documenting Indicator 8 (Struktureret patientuddannelse, or "structured patient education") within the AFDK program administered by Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram. This chapter builds the evidence base for patient education as an integrated part of AF treatment, drawing on European ESC guidelines and Danish national recommendations, and it also describes the ABC Pathway model for integrated AF care — covering stroke prevention (A), better symptom control (B), and reduction of cardiovascular risk (C). Lunde et al.'s 2018 research is invoked specifically to justify individualized approaches to patient education within this broader framework [^src1].

No further biographical, institutional, or relational details about Lunde et al. are available in the corpus. The entry is thin: it consists of a single citation used to support a point about individualized patient education in AF care.

## Mentions

- Page 97: "AF er en kompleks sygdom, der påvirker patienter forskelligt. Den sundhedsprofessionelle skal derfor være opmærksom på, at patienter har et individuelt udgangspunkt for at tilegne sig læring og færdigheder (Lunde et al., 2018)" [^src1]
